Bill number: HB1740
<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 1740

 By Glynn

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to the Individualized Education Act.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1402(3), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (3) "Eligible student" means a resident of this state who:

 (A)

 (i) Is a child with any of the following disabilities as defined by the

 state board of education pursuant to § 49-10-102:

 (a) Autism;

 (b) Deaf-blindness;

 (c) Hearing impairments;

 (d) Intellectual disability;

 (e) Orthopedic impairments;

 (f) Traumatic brain injury;

 (g) Visual impairments;

 (h) Developmental delay;

 (i) Multiple disabilities;

 (j) A specific learning disability; or

 (k) Deafness;

 (ii) Has an active individualized education program (IEP) in

 accordance with 34 C.F.R. § 300 et seq., § 49-10-102, and regulations of

 the state board of education with one (1) of the disabilities pursuant to

 subdivision (3)(A)(i) as the primary or secondary disability in effect at the

 time the department receives the request for participation in the program;

 and

 (iii) Meets at least one (1) of the following requirements:

 (a) Was previously enrolled in and attended a Tennessee

 public school for the one (1) full school year immediately

 preceding the school year in which the student receives an

 individualized education account (IEA);

 (b) Is enrolling in a Tennessee school for the first time; or

 (c) Received an individualized education account (IEA) in

 the previous school year; or

 (B)

 (i) Is a child with a medical condition that inhibits the child from

 attending school in person, as determined by the state board of

 education; and

 (ii) Is entitled to attend a public school;

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1402(6), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (6) "Participating school" means:

 (A) A nonpublic school that meets the requirements established in this

 part and seeks to enroll eligible students; or

 (B) For an eligible student, as defined in subdivision (3)(B), a home

 school, as defined in § 49-6-3050(a)(1);

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1404, is amended by adding

the following as a new subsection:

 (d) This section does not apply to an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-

 1402(3)(B), or a participating school, as defined in § 49-10-1402(6)(B).

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1403(d), is amended by

adding ", as defined in § 49-10-1402(6)(A)," after "A participating school".

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1405(a)(7), is amended by

adding ", as defined in § 49-10-1402(6)(A)," after "of participating schools".

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 10, Part 14, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) A parent of an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-1402(3)(B), shall ensure

 that funds in an IEA are used only for approved expenses listed in § 49-10-1403(b).

 (b) The department shall create and implement a process to ensure that funds in

 an IEA for an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-1402(3)(B), are regularly monitored

 to ensure compliance with this section and § 49-10-1403(b).

 (c) The department may suspend or terminate an eligible student from

 participating in the program, if the department determines that the parent has failed to

 comply with the requirements of this section. If the department terminates an eligible

 student's participation in the program pursuant to this subsection (c), then the student is

 ineligible from participating in the program in the future.

 SECTION 7. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would change who can qualify for a Tennessee individualized education account (IEA) and allow a home school to participate for certain students. It would take effect July 1, 2026.

A Tennessee resident could qualify through one of two paths. Under the disability path, the student would need one of the listed disabilities, an active individualized education program (IEP) naming one of those disabilities as a primary or secondary disability when the department receives the request, and either a full year of attendance at a Tennessee public school immediately before receiving an IEA, first-time enrollment in a Tennessee school, or an IEA in the previous school year. Under the other path, the student would need a medical condition that the state board of education determines prevents in-person school attendance and must be entitled to attend a public school.

For a student qualifying through the medical-condition path, a home school could be a participating school. Those students and home schools would be exempt from the requirements in § 49-10-1404; the bill does not show those requirements. The bill would also specify that references to participating schools in two other provisions refer to nonpublic participating schools.

A parent of a student qualifying through the medical-condition path would have to use IEA funds only for the approved expenses listed in § 49-10-1403(b). The department would have to regularly monitor those funds for compliance. It could suspend or terminate a student's participation if the parent fails to comply. A student whose participation is terminated on that basis could not participate again.
</summary>

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1405(a)(7), is amended by

claims.rationale: Both amendments restrict the references to subdivision (6)(A), which defines the nonpublic-school category.

claims.claim: A parent of a medical-condition-path student must ensure IEA funds are used only for approved expenses listed in Section 49-10-1403(b).
claims.summary_quote: A parent of a student qualifying through the medical-condition path would have to use IEA funds only for the approved expenses listed in § 49-10-1403(b).
claims.source_quote:
A parent of an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-1402(3)(B), shall ensure

 that funds in an IEA are used only for approved expenses listed in § 49-10-1403(b).
claims.rationale: The summary conveys the parent's mandatory approved-expense restriction.

claims.claim: The department must ensure regular compliance monitoring of those funds.
claims.summary_quote: The department would have to regularly monitor those funds for compliance.
claims.source_quote:
The department shall create and implement a process to ensure that funds in

 an IEA for an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-1402(3)(B), are regularly monitored

 to ensure compliance with this section and § 49-10-1403(b).
claims.rationale: The bill mandates a departmental process ensuring regular compliance monitoring.

claims.claim: The department may suspend a student's participation for parental noncompliance.
claims.summary_quote: It could suspend or terminate a student's participation if the parent fails to comply.
claims.source_quote:
The department may suspend or terminate an eligible student from

 participating in the program, if the department determines that the parent has failed to

 comply with the requirements of this section.
claims.rationale: Suspension is discretionary and conditioned on the department's determination of parental noncompliance.

claims.claim: The department may terminate a student's participation for parental noncompliance.
claims.summary_quote: It could suspend or terminate a student's participation if the parent fails to comply.
claims.source_quote:
The department may suspend or terminate an eligible student from

 participating in the program, if the department determines that the parent has failed to

 comply with the requirements of this section.
claims.rationale: Termination is also an authorized discretionary response to that noncompliance.

claims.claim: A student terminated on that basis cannot participate in the future.
claims.summary_quote: A student whose participation is terminated on that basis could not participate again.
claims.source_quote:
If the department terminates an eligible

 student's participation in the program pursuant to this subsection (c), then the student is

 ineligible from participating in the program in the future.
claims.rationale: The future-participation bar expressly follows termination under this subsection.
